title: latency-premium-per-user-brain-dump
content:
Quick brain dump on a potential "latency premium" add-on + per-user gating. Not polished — mostly back-of-envelope math and open questions.

Context / motivation:
- We get a lot of feature requests from product teams: some customers need consistently low p99 for interactive experiences (chat UIs, assistants) and are willing to pay a premium for reserved low-latency capacity.
- Current levers: Dedicated capacity, model routing, smaller context windows, batching controls. But those are coarse and expensive to provision per-customer.
- Idea: Offer a lightweight per-seat/per-route "latency premium" which guarantees a tighter latency SLA by routing priority to hot pools and enabling aggressive caching/bypass for eligible requests. Could be a per-seat monthly surcharge + per-token uplift.

Goals for this note:
- Sketch unit economics (when does this make sense for us?)
- Check customer value signals + price anchors
- Outline implementation constraints and simplest MVP product surface

Assumptions (rough):
- Baseline hosted API cost to us for avg token: $0.0006 per output token (weighted across model mixes). (assume a mix of 13B/34B quantized and a small percent of LLM-70B bursts)
- Baseline latency pool (best-effort) p95 = 300ms, p99 = 620ms for interactive tokens.
- Hot fast-path pool unit cost (reserved GPUs, pinned slices, higher ops) = 2.6x baseline per-token cost (so ~ $0.00156/token). This is because smaller batches, pre-warmed KV caches, and fewer multiplexed contexts.
- Typical customer interactive use: 300 tokens generated per session on avg, 3 sessions per user per day -> 900 tokens/user/day -> ~27k tokens/user/month.
- Target margin target for add-on: at least 40% GP after infra and support overhead.

Back-of-envelope pricing levers:
1) Flat per-seat surcharge (monthly) to keep things predictable.
2) Per-token uplift for tokens routed through fast-path (could be a % multiplier or absolute add-on).
3) Enrollment criteria (min users, min monthly spend) to avoid fragmentation and tiny customers causing overhead.

Scenario A — Per-seat + token uplift (favored MVP):
- Charge $6/user/month + 20% per-token uplift over standard hosted token price.
- For a user generating 27k tokens/month: base token cost (charged to customer at list) = 27k * $0.0006 = $16.20. Uplift adds 20% = $3.24. Seat surcharge = $6 -> total incremental paid = $9.24 -> customer pays $25.44 more than base.
- Our incremental cost for those tokens if routed to fast-path: 27k * $0.00156 = $42.12. Baseline cost would have been 27k * $0.0006 = $16.20, so incremental infra cost = $25.92. We charge the customer an extra $9.24 but incur $25.92 -> not profitable. Oops. Need to adjust.

Observation: Per-token uplift must cover most of the incremental infra cost. Either increase % uplift or increase seat surcharge. Alternatively, limit fast-path to a fraction of tokens (e.g., only prefix/first X tokens per session or only p95-sensitive requests).

Scenario B — Higher uplift + usage floor:
- Charge $12/user/month + 120% per-token uplift. For 27k tokens: token uplift = 27k * 0.0006 * 1.2 = $19.44. Seat = $12 -> incremental paid = $31.44. Incremental infra cost = $25.92 -> margin ~ 17% on the addon (before overhead). Better but might be a tough sell.

Scenario C — Hybrid: fast-path for first N tokens per session (e.g., first 80 tokens) + reduced uplift thereafter. Rationale: UX critical at start of conversation (first impressions), tail tokens can be cheaper.
- If avg session=300 tokens, and we protect first 80 tokens only: protected tokens/user/month = 80 * 3 * 30 = 7200 tokens. Infra incremental cost for protected = 7200 * (0.00156-0.0006) = 7200 * 0.00096 = $6.912.
- Charge $6/user/month + per-protected-token uplift of $0.0009 (rounded). For 7200 tokens, uplift = $6.48 + seat $6 = $12.48 incremental collected vs $6.912 cost -> good margin. Rest of tokens stay on standard pool.
- This is attractive because it targets UX-sensitive portion and reduces our overall infra burden.

Other gating / anti-abuse considerations:
- Must prevent customers from routing large batch offline jobs through fast-path. Enforce route-level flags and per-route QPS limits.
- Enrollment requires verification and opt-in per route + default rate caps (e.g., 50 qps per customer unless dedicated).
- Offer a trial period with limited token allowance (e.g., 50k protected tokens) to prove value.

Implementation MVP (minimal):
- Product surface: toggle on console per-route "latency premium" with seat count and per-route cap. Pricing UI shows per-seat + per-protected-token uplift and an estimate based on historical usage.
- Runtime: mark eligible requests with header X-RW-LATENCY-PREMIUM -> router picks priority queue. Implement fast-path that accepts only up to N tokens per session (configurable) and rejects/rewrites others.
- Billing: flag tokens that hit fast-path and bill uplift per token. Seat surcharge billed monthly.

Customer value signals to validate with sales/CS:
- Are customers willing to pay >$6-12/user/mo for better p99? Which segments? (SaaS productivity tools, customer support, live agents)
- Do customers care more about per-seat SLA or per-route guarantees?
- Which UX thresholds matter? p95 150ms vs p95 300ms vs p99 250ms?

Open questions / TODOs:
- Real incremental cost figure: 2.6x is a placeholder. Need infra to run real perf delta experiment with representative models and batch curves. Ticketed: JIRA-PLT-1987 for perf run.
- How often will customers actually hit the protected tokens limit? Need distribution of session token lengths (ask analytics team).
- Legal / SLA wording and compensation model for misses (crediting).
- Support cost: will this cause more support tickets due to perceived slowdown or mis-configuration? Estimate $/seat overhead.

Quick next steps:
- Ask infra for real per-token cost delta for hot-path vs baseline (small perf job). -> JIRA-PLT-1987 assigned to Diego.
- Pull session length histogram for interactive routes (last 90 days) -> analytics.
- Mock pricing UI and send to 2 AE contacts for feedback.
- Prototype runtime header + router flag in staging, gated feature flag.

Notes-to-self:
- Prefer hybrid (protect first-X tokens) as it aligns costs with UX and is much more defensible economically.
- Consider adding "fast-path burst credits" for occasional spikes (like 100k credits/month) as an add-on for customers who don't want per-seat.
- Keep product naming neutral — "latency premium" vs "priority latency" vs "interactive SLA". Run a quick survey.

End of rough notes. Not ready to present yet. Save and revisit after perf numbers and session histograms come back.

References and links I scribbled during meeting:
- conv-session-hist-analytics (ask analytics)

summary: Personal scratchpad exploring a per-user "latency premium" pricing add-on. Includes three pricing scenarios, back-of-envelope math, implementation MVP, open questions, and next steps.
